<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **152** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **60** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `aa18d08ed2bbedafc2ea6b82aafba95167544c42` — the merge of head `bd40928d9b6a68c34b831329fb941ada16eed291` into base `fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin aa18d08ed2bbedafc2ea6b82aafba95167544c42 && git checkout aa18d08ed2bbedafc2ea6b82aafba95167544c42
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048 bd40928d9b6a68c34b831329fb941ada16eed291 && git checkout -B drift-repro fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048 && git merge --no-ff bd40928d9b6a68c34b831329fb941ada16eed291

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fc5913e117405814e5c40e4e9bbe6b2da7420048` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T14:05Z

Head-sha: 29905cc9e03331d66f4c9ebac4a53a42e855b20a
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34764 (claim 6946560350, amended 6949721949; os-dev report 6948894102; live round eval-run #34842).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Part of #34764`, with no closing verb. That is right, because the eval lane's charter line is the seat's own PR and lands after this one. Five commits; fix round 1 is `2f33c265`..`29905cc9`.

**Scope vs claim.** All 12 paths sit inside the amended claim:
- new files under `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/**` and `test/skill-evals/**`;
- one `scripts` entry in `packages/qa/scenarios/package.json`;
- the package README section;
- one changeset;
- the one `COMPOUND_ANCHOR_LEDGER` row in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.data.mjs`, which the amendment added.

`runner/driver.ts` and `runner/cli.ts` are untouched.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in the body and the changeset, and they agree.
- `files[]` is `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, so `src/skill-evals/**` never ships.
- `bin`, `exports` and the tsup entries are unchanged. The body's dist probe finds `gradeAnswer` in 0 files, against a control of 8.
- What a consumer installs changes by README text and a `scripts` key. `@objectstack/scenarios` at `patch` is right.

There is no contract face, so no seat L2 is owed.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34841`: 0 of 12 paths, NOT governed, 1924 lines (under 3000).

**Check-runs at 29905cc9.** 53 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all 10 shards, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (it reads the new ledger row), `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Validate Package Dependencies`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. The UI legs were skipped by path filter.

**Login guard.** `subscriptionOnlyEnv`, `assertSubscriptionLogin` and `effortLevelsFromHelp` are imported from `runner/driver.ts`, not copied. In `cli.ts`, `preflight()` runs before the skills source is resolved and before any turn. `--dry-run`, `--regrade` and `--self-test` skip it and ask no model. The CLI refusal test asserts the stand-in `claude` is never asked a turn and no `--out` is created, and the ablation (the preflight call replaced with a constant) turned it red. Every turn is spawned without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` (pinned).

**Arms.** The arms' argv is identical except for the copied bundle:
- `--setting-sources project`, `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Skill`, `--allowedTools Skill`;
- an empty `--mcp-config` with `--strict-mcp-config`;
- `--no-session-persistence`.

The with-skill copy filters `evals/` (both the directory and its descendants) and dereferences links, so no path leads back into the checkout. The two isolation claims the README makes were measured on 2.1.326: a user skill is absent under `--setting-sources project`, and a read outside the turn's directory is refused in `-p`.

**Verdicts.** `verdictOf` gives four outcomes:
- `error` when the process fails, there is no init line, or there is no `success` result;
- `invalid` when the arm is wrong: a with-skill turn whose init line lacks a listed bundle, or a no-skill turn that lists or launches a catalog bundle;
- otherwise literal case-sensitive token grading.

`invalid` and `error` stay out of the denominator and are counted and named. The `user-invocable: false` handling (graded, with `armEvidence: launched | not-shown`) is the measured fix for the 34 `objectui` turns.

**Quota stop.** The round stops at `rejected` or at utilization ≥ `--max-utilization`. Turns not run are recorded as not run, and the command exits 3.

**Docs made false?** None. The README section is new and its cost and time figures are this PR's round (418/418, 56 min, 0.45 → 0.56). Nothing else documents a `skill-evals` command.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. `--regrade` re-scores old answers against whatever the workspace cases say now, and the regraded record does not say so.**
  - `regradeRound` checks only that the skills source label matches (`workspace skills/`). It then grades each recorded answer with today's `skills/BUNDLE/evals/*.json` (`byKey.get(rec.key)`).
  - The round never records which case text it ran: not a skills or evals hash, and not the assertions per record. Only `runner.sha` is recorded, which is HEAD plus a dirty flag.
  - So a round from week N, regraded after a case's `must_contain` or `prompt` changed, mixes week-N answers with week-N+1 assertions. The header still reads "applies the current rules … no model asked", and `changed` counts those flips as if they were rule changes.
  - That is not hypothetical: #34789 is rewording over-literal assertions across `skills/*/evals/**`, and this runner's first users will regrade around it.
  - A small fix closes it. Record a hash of each case as run (prompt plus both token lists) on each run record, or one evals-tree hash on `round.json`. On `--regrade`, either refuse a case whose hash differs, or regrade it and count and name those cases apart in the `regraded` line (`N verdict(s) differ; M case(s) changed since the round`). Add a pin for each.
  - `--skills-from VERSION` is immutable and unaffected.

Under the current merge standard this gets fixed before landing. I'll take the delta read.

### Notes
- N1. `COMPOUND_ANCHOR_LEDGER` prose now says 290 bare plus 36 compound out of "324 code-position matches". 290 + 36 is 326, and the 324 was already one short at 35. The 36 rows and 29 spellings check out against the table (I counted 36 and 29). Only the 324 is stale. Nothing pins it, so fix it if you touch the file again.
- N2. The 144 permission denials across 111 turns in #34842's round are recorded by count only. This head records each refused tool's name (`deniedTools`). The next round can say whether any denial was a reach for files outside the turn, the only way the no-skill arm could see a bundle.
- N3. `no-skill ≥ with-skill` counts both-fail cases (63 of them this round). The README and summary both say so. When the eval lane reads regressions, both-fail rows belong with the #34789 assertion carrier, not with skill value.

Next: o3-F fixes S1, then the L1-c delta read. No seat L2 is owed, and o3-F lands after the delta.

## L1: ACCEPT (delta) · 2026-11-17T15:32Z

Head-sha: bd40928d9b6a68c34b831329fb941ada16eed291
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c. This is a delta read of `29905cc9`..`bd40928d` against my 6950349685 (os-dev report 6951964966).

### 席位核对

**Delta.** Three commits, 7 files, +248/-29, all inside the claimed surface: `src/skill-evals/{cases,cli,run,self-test}.ts`, the test, the README paragraph and the ledger prose. Nothing moved into `bin`, `exports` or `files[]`. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` still hold. Not governed (0 of 12 paths), 2147 lines in all.

**Check-runs at bd40928d.** 57 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all 10 shards, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`.

**S1 (regrade against reworded cases): closed.**
- **The hash.** `hashCase` is sha256 over `JSON.stringify([prompt, mustContain, mustNotContain])`, which is what a turn is sent plus what it is graded on. `expected_output` is left out, correctly. `judgeTurn` stamps it on every new record.
- **Changed and removed cases.** `regradeRecords` sets apart, as a whole case, any case whose recorded hash differs from today's or that left the catalog (including a whole bundle that left). Its record files are not rewritten. They are out of `cases`, so out of every rate, and the `regraded` line names them. As a second fence, `regradeRecord` throws on a changed case if anything calls it directly.
- **Unhashed and added cases.** Unhashed records (the whole 11-17 round) are regraded and counted, and the line says plainly that nothing shows those are the cases that ran. Added cases are left out, not counted as not run.
- **Repeated regrades.** `plannedKeys` unions the summary's cases with any earlier `setApart`, so a case set apart once and later restored comes back on the next regrade.
- **Pins and ablation.** Four new tests (hash scope, same / changed / unhashed, removed / added, and the command end to end with record bytes kept), a new self-test row with the floor raised from 20 to 21, and an ablation leg in the report.

Choosing set-apart over refusing the whole regrade is the better option, because it keeps pre-#34789 rounds regradable without mixing in old answers.

**N1 (census prose): closed.** 330 = 294 bare + 36 compound, 21 under `ui/`. The 36 rows and 29 spellings match the table.

**The dev's carrier note.** The bundle list and `user-invocable` flags are still read from today's tree, so a flip there shows up in the `changed` count instead of being set apart. That is acceptable: those flags decide arm validity, not grading, and a flip is rare and visible in `regradedFrom`. Not owed.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
None new.

Next: o3-F lands. No seat L2 is owed. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
